title: Cross-tenant temporary pin exchange protocol
body:
Summary:
This doc proposes an operational protocol for safely enabling and reversing temporary cross-tenant region pins ("temporary pin exchange") when customers require short-lived data processing across regions (e.g., emergency analytics, partner integrations, regulatory exception windows). The goal is to provide a clear, auditable path for SRE/ops and account teams to execute requests with minimal risk to residency SLAs and auditability.

Scope and constraints:
- Applies only to tenants with an existing hard region pin (tenant_pin != null).
- Temporary exchange must be explicitly approved by legal/compliance for any cross-border movement.
- Max duration by default: 72 hours. Extensions require escalation and documented justification.
- Only data buckets tagged as "shareable-temporary" are eligible. Highly sensitive data (PCI/PHI) excluded unless explicit contract addendum.

Definitions:
- Requesting tenant: origin tenant that requests temporary inbound/outbound processing.
- Host region: region where the tenant's pinned data currently resides.
- Exchange target: the other region/tenant that will run processing.
- Pin exchange record: auditable record (DB + signed ticket) capturing who approved, timeline, buckets, and fallback plan.

Prerequisites (ops checklist before enabling):
1) Legal signoff: confirmation email or JIRA approval from legal/compliance (attach to pin exchange record).
2) Customer acknowledgment: signed or accepted temporary cross-border terms (email template below).
3) Telemetry toggles: enable enhanced residency audit logging for the tenant for the exchange window.
4) Backup snapshot: take immutable snapshot(s) of affected buckets prior to any movement.
5) Capacity reservation: confirm compute capacity in exchange target region (avoid noisy neighbor failures).

High-level flow:
1) Customer or AE submits JIRA/Request ticket with template fields (tenant id, requested target region, buckets, business reason, start/end window, legal doc id).
2) Product-ops triage: validate eligibility (tag checks, SLA tier, data sensitivity).
3) Legal/compliance review: approve or deny with comments.
4) SRE schedules maintenance window and capacity reservation. Post-link created ticket in pin exchange record.
5) Execute exchange steps (see operator script).
6) Post-exchange verification: telemetry review, integrity checks, rollback test.
7) Close pin exchange record, attach audit artifacts and customer notice.

Operator script (detailed steps):
- Step 0: Preconditions validated in ticket and recorded in pin exchange record.
- Step 1: Mark tenant as "exchange-in-progress" in tenancy control-plane (this sets more aggressive logging and temporarily disables automatic evictions).
- Step 2: Export minimal metadata map for affected buckets (object ids, checksums, ACLs). Record checksums.
- Step 3: Using secure transfer subsystem, copy objects to exchange target region into an isolated namespace with an enforced TTL matching requested window. All transfers MUST use tenant-specific KMS keys where applicable.
- Step 4: At target region, spin up a transient processing pool assigned to the temporary namespace. Attach ephemeral credentials scoped to only the namespace and processing job.
- Step 5: Run processing under customer-supplied container or internal job, stream outputs back (where required) to a "results-only" bucket in host region or to a designated partner endpoint per contract.
- Step 6: Perform integrity verification: object count and checksum match, logs shipped to immutable audit store, and privacy guardrails (PII filters) executed.
- Step 7: Tear down compute and delete copied objects per TTL policy. Keep audit trail and snapshots for retention window.

Rollback procedure (if integrity or policy violation detected):
- Immediate freeze: mark tenant status to "exchange-failed" and revoke all ephemeral credentials.
- Halt processing: kill jobs and isolate any outputs produced.
- Restore: if any mutative write occurred to host region buckets, use pre-exchange snapshots to revert. Document differences.
- Forensic capture: preserve exchange target region state in immutable storage and notify legal + security.
- Customer comms: inform customer and affected partners, escalate to oncall as needed.

Telemetry and audit requirements:
- Pin exchange record must include: approver ids, timestamps for start/end, snapshot ids, transfer job ids, checksum manifests, and legal doc reference.
- Enable high-frequency residency logs (token-level sampling) for duration + 30 days.
- Emit an exchange-stats event with metrics: bytes transferred, objects transferred, transfer latency percentile, CPU-hours used, and error counts.
- Postmortem: if any anomaly > 0.1% error rate observed (transfer integrity or access violations), require SRE postmortem and legal review.

Testing checklist (pre-launch):
- Dry run with synthetic tenant and synthetic data set mapped to same tags.
- Chaos test: simulate mid-transfer host-region outage and verify rollback path triggers cleanly.
- Scale test: run parallel exchange tasks to confirm capacity reservation behavior.
- Permission audit: verify ephemeral credentials only allow listed actions in target region.

Customer communications (short templates):
- Initial approval confirmation (to attach to ticket):
  "Thanks — we have approved your temporary cross-region processing window from {start} to {end}. Work will be executed under account {ops-request-id}. Please confirm no additional buckets are required. Legal approval: {legal-doc-id}."
- Post-exchange closure notice:
  "Your temporary processing window completed at {end}. Transfer bytes: {bytes}. We retained audit snapshots for {retention-days} days. Contact support@redwood.ai with questions or to request extensions."

Risk considerations and mitigations:
- Risk: inadvertent exposure of non-eligible objects. Mitigation: pre-transfer tag enforcement and post-transfer object ACL checks.
- Risk: capacity shortage in target region causing partial transfer. Mitigation: mandatory capacity reservation + pre-transfer quota lock.
- Risk: legal pushback on precedent. Mitigation: require legal signoff and unique justification logged for each exchange (avoid template approvals).

Open questions and action items:
- Q: Should we limit the number of concurrent temporary exchanges per region? Action: engineering to propose region-level throttles (ENG-4922).
- Q: How long must we retain transfer manifests for audit beyond customer-requested retention? Action: compliance to confirm retention floor.
- Action: Add UI affordance in Console to request and show exchange status (product ticket PROD-308).

Appendix: quick operator script (CLI snippets)
- create-record: redwood-ctl exchange create --tenant {tid} --target-region eu-west1 --buckets bkt1,bkt2 --window 2025-01-10T00:00Z/2025-01-13T00:00Z --legal-id CONF-123
- reserve-capacity: redwood-ctl region reserve --region eu-west1 --units 32 --policy exchange-temp-{tid}
- start-transfer: redwood-transfer --src bkt1 --dst eu-west1:tmp/{tid}/bkt1 --kms-key projects/{p}/locations/{loc}/keyRings/{kr}/cryptoKeys/{k}

References and tickets:
- JIRA ENG-4821 (temporary pin exchange RFC)
- Confluence: /residency/protocols/temp-pin-exchange (detailed legal checklist)
- Slack: #prod-residency-thread-5f3c (design discussion)

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep default window small. We should start with internal beta with 3 pilot customers. Mateo to own pilot coordination.
- Ensure metrics are in Redwood Console drilldown under tenant -> residency -> exchanges.
summary_notes: Draft operational protocol for temporary cross-tenant pin exchanges. Focus on auditability, minimal blast radius, and legal guardrails. Pilot recommended.
